Through: Mr. Ashwani Tyagi, Adv
 Petitioners in person.

versus
 The State (Nct Of Delhi) And Ors. ...

Through: Mr. Raj Kumar, APP for  with SI Neeti, P.S.Jah  Mr. Rohit and Mr. Gaur  Advocate for responden  Respondent no.2 in per  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJNISH BHATNAGAR  ORDER % 20.03.2023 1.
This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No. 715/2016, under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Jahangirpuri, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.

Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 15.01.2016 according to Hindu rites and customs and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
After the marriage, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 26.09.2016.
On 19.12.2016, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, with the intervention of elderly persons, the respondent no. 2 and petitioner no. 1 have settled the matter amicably and they started living together since August 2018.
One male child was born on 29.03.2021 and female child was born on 24.01.2022.
In this regard settlement is already on record dated 17.08.2022.

Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been Mohit Mittal And Ors vs The State (Nct Of Delhi) And Ors on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158722730/

sentences.text: identified by their counsels.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent no.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioner no. 1 and she is living happily with her husband.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
Respondent no.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

5. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement and as the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are living happily together, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and of FIR No. 715/2016,
under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Jahangirpuri, and all proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
7.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J MARCH 20, 2023/ib
